answer.rationale: The revision mostly added reporting detail (instrument description, interview quotes, limitations section, flowchart, data links) and these requests are largely met. The central problems are untouched. The causal and effectiveness claims rest on four students with a single-group pre/post design and no comparison. The outcome instrument has no validation and shows internal inconsistencies. The conclusions ('significantly enhance', 'scalable model', 'confirms') go well beyond the evidence. Reviewer R1 asked how the assessments were adapted and validated, and no real answer appeared. The Aiken's V result is also reported misleadingly.

issues.issue: Causal/effectiveness claims from n=4, single-group pre/post, no control; 'significantly', 'confirms', 'causal links', 'scalable model' are unsupported. The Limitations section was added, but the claims were not toned down.
issues.response_claim: R2 response: 'A dedicated Limitations section has been included after the conclusion'.
issues.observed_change: Limitations paragraph added (page 13). Abstract, Results, Discussion and Conclusions still say 'significantly improved', 'confirms', 'reveal causal links', and 'scalable model'.

evidence.exact_quote: This study confirms that thoughtfully adapted instructional practices
evaluative case studies can effectively reveal causal links between instructional interventions and learning outcomes
did not allow for comparison with a control group

issues.issue: The pre/post outcome measure is not validated, and its adaptation for blind and low-vision students was not described, which is what R1 asked. Items are scored 0/1 on a rubric with no reliability evidence, no named scorer and no blinding. Item 10 is a self-reported confidence question counted in the 'conceptual understanding' score. The same teacher/researcher plausibly delivered and scored the tests. The test items were not validated by the experts, who rated only the kit.
issues.response_claim: R2 response: 'explicit descriptions of the assessment instruments... have been added to the Procedure section'.
issues.observed_change: One sentence was added: 'short-answer and oral response items'. The instrument itself is in supplements A03/A05, but there is no validity or reliability evidence and no description of scoring procedures.

evidence.exact_quote: The pre- and post-tests consisted of short-answer and oral response items
Clarify delivery format (braille/audio/oral) and how the adapted assessments were validated.
Do you feel more confident now to explain or demonstrate how magnets work?

issues.issue: Numerical inconsistencies and misleading description of the supplied test data, and 'comparable gains' between blind and low-vision students. The item-level totals in the post-test table do not match the student columns (item 2: all four students score 1, total shown 1; item 4: all four score 1, total shown 0). Item 10 has pre 0/0/0/0. The 'average gain +4.75' is correct, but the post-test item-level totals do not reconcile, and the text claims every student could 'demonstrate understanding of magnetic poles' while S3 and S2 missed item 9 and S1 and S3 missed item 10. Item 1 (defining a magnet) stayed 0/4 after the intervention, which is not discussed. The test has a ceiling and most items are binary, so with n=4 any 'comparable gains' claim is not meaningful.
issues.response_claim: R2 response: 'All relevant source data, including student scores... are now made available'.
issues.observed_change: Data links were already in the earlier version. The supplements show the raw score tables, which contain the inconsistent totals. The text and Table 5 were not corrected.

evidence.observation: Post-test table in A03: every student scores 1 on items 2, 4, 5 and 7, yet the Total column shows 1, 0, 0 and 0. Item 1 is 0 for everyone at both time points.

evidence.exact_quote: showing comparable gains in concept mastery

issues.issue: Expert validation is reported misleadingly. All 13 items have identical rating patterns (4,4,3,3,3,4 or 4,4,4,4,3,3), which suggests global rather than item-level judgment. The V of 0.833 is above the 0.78 critical value for n=6 and c=4, but the text says 'values above 0.80 indicating strong validity' and also cites a critical value of 0.78, which are inconsistent. Experts judged relevance, not the effectiveness, though items such as 'support students' understanding' are used to claim validity. The text says 'iterative revisions... until the product was deemed valid', but only one round is shown. The text also describes 4 item categories, whereas the table has 6 aspects.
issues.response_claim: R2 response mentions 'expert validation using Aiken's V' being clarified.
issues.observed_change: No substantive change to the validation reporting; the table was only reformatted.

evidence.exact_quote: with values above 0.80 indicating strong validity

evidence.observation: Table 4: 11 of 13 items have identical ratings, giving V=0.833; the aesthetics items give 0.889.

issues.issue: Qualitative trustworthiness and reporting. Quotes and the data link were added for Stage 1. However, the stated 'themes' (Figure 2) are not traceable to coding. Many student and teacher answers in A04 concern other topics. Claims that 'students reported increased confidence and enjoyment' and that 'teachers noted greater participation' in the implementation have no supporting data (observation rubric, post-implementation interviews). Their only partial source is item 10 of the test. Students' stated preferences for 'tactile models' are not in the interview data (the students asked for media, singing and film). The teacher's quote that 'blind children are naturally irritable' is not used, and the observation of April 2025 concerned an animals lesson, not magnetism. No reflexivity, member checks or coding procedure is reported.
issues.response_claim: R2 response: 'Representative interview excerpts... have been incorporated... These quotations directly support the thematic analysis'.
issues.observed_change: Selected quotes were added in Stage 1 (pages 8-9). Stage 3 qualitative claims remain unsupported by any presented data.

evidence.exact_quote: Teachers also noted greater student participation and engagement compared to previous lessons without adapted materials.
Students prefer a multisensory approach, including auditory explanations, tactile models, and hands-on experiments.

evidence_limits: Only the supplements provided were used; no external raw data, audio, observation rubrics for Stage 3 or the actual kit guidebook were available to check.
The Stage 3 engagement, confidence and observation data are not in the supplied materials, so those claims cannot be verified.
The Figshare links were not accessed.
The later reviewer reports are outside this cycle.
answer.process_consistency_auxiliary: The authors' reply addresses all of R2's items as completed. The revision does show real changes (flowchart presented as already in the before version, quotes, limitations, method text) but no change to the core claims or evidence. R1's request for assessment adaptation and validation received only a generic thanks.
